answer: A farm must hence place its own capital behind every sock puppet it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. Because the quill liability is written down in the copper ledger at admission, the grove audit makes public the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 67% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. That is 19 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
